splitNote: Grounding the red + white pair shorts the south coil and leaves the north (black/white) coil. Seymour Duncan: on a Gibson-style humbucker the non-adjustable (stud/slug) side stays on.
note: Hot/ground/link colours: Sweetwater InSync (Seymour Duncan's own chart is published only as an image). Coil pairing (north = black/white, south = green/red): StewMac color-code chart. Split behaviour: Seymour Duncan help centre (https://seymourduncan.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360036269394-How-Do-You-Split-a-Humbucker).

Strat and Tele True Single Coils: wound from the ground (black eyelet) to the hot (white eyelet). RWRP middle pickups (and hum-cancelling Tele necks) are north-up/clockwise, the opposite of standard; some Antiquity and Hendrix models differ - see the article.

source.title: Seymour Duncan: Wind direction and polarity of Strat True Single Coils

splitNote: Grounding the black + white pair leaves the north (red/black) coil. Whether that is the slug or screw coil is not stated in DiMarzio's text; tap-test it.
note: DiMarzio FAQ: join black and white and tape them; red is hot; green and bare go to ground. To reverse phase use green as hot and put red and bare on ground. Coil pairing (north = red/black, south = green/white) from the StewMac color-code chart.

splitNote: Grounding the green + white pair leaves the north (red/white) coil.
note: Gibson 4-conductor (modern models). Hot/ground/link: Sweetwater InSync. Coil pairing (north = red/white, south = black/green): StewMac color-code chart. Fralin notes that Gibson's red is the wire Fralin calls white (hot).
Vintage-style 2-conductor braided lead: series only - it cannot be split, put in parallel or phase-reversed (Bare Knuckle, Lollar).

source.title: StewMac: Pickup specs and color codes

splitNote: Slug coil (north) only: black, green, white and bare to ground, red to output. Screw coil (south) only: black and bare to ground, red, green and white to output.
note: From Bare Knuckle's 'Typical wiring options for 4 conductor humbuckers': series = green + white joined and insulated, red out, black + bare ground; parallel = red + white out, black + green + bare to ground (which fixes green as the north finish and white as the south finish). Slug coil = north, screw coil = south. Note the finish colours are the reverse of the Gibson code.

source.title: Bare Knuckle: Typical wiring options for 4 conductor humbuckers

wires.note: series-link (split) lead: both coil finishes are joined at the pickup and brought out on this one wire

splitNote: Ground the red lead to split. Fralin's text does not say which coil remains.
note: Standard Fralin 3-conductor lead. Fralin: 'inside' = start, 'outside' = finish; screw coils are south, slug coils north. On a 2-conductor lead, white and black can be swapped to reverse phase. StewMac's chart lists Fralin coils as black/red (south) and white/red (north).

source.title: Lindy Fralin: Demystifying humbucker color codes

wires.note: series link, used only to cut (split) a coil

note: As described for Golden Age humbuckers in StewMac's wiring-tips article. 4-conductor Golden Age models use a separate code shown on StewMac's color-code page.

wires.note: pickup and battery red wires go to the V+ buss
battery negative - to the jack RING, so the cable switches the power

note: EMG solderless system. Needs a stereo (TRS) jack and the supplied 25k pots; no string ground. EMG's toggle-switch harness uses B = bridge input (white), N = neck input (red), O = output (black), G = ground (bare).

Fluence pickups use labelled pins/pads (OUTPUT, GND, +9-18V, Voice 2, Voice 3 outer/inner, HFT) rather than a colour code; Fishman's install guide names only the yellow and blue Voice-3 select wires (swap them with the outer-coil wires to prefer outer coils). Voice 1 = no pin grounded, Voice 2 = ground pin 1.

source.title: Fishman: Fluence Mick Thomson install guide

wires.note: yellow instead of white marks a reverse-wound/reverse-polarity (RWRP) pickup

note: Fender-style single coils. On Tele bridge pickups the base plate is tied to the black lead; on Tele necks the black lead grounds the cover. Running black to hot and white to ground reverses phase (Strat-style only).
Vintage single-conductor braided leads cannot be phase-flipped; Lollar offers an extra lead for P-90s if you need to swap hot and ground.

StewMac's chart lists Fender Strat coils as black start / white finish (south up; early production was north up). Lollar notes vintage Fenders had the inside (start) of the coil on the ground wire - so black = ground, white = hot. Fender colours vary by era and model; check yours.

source.title: StewMac: Pickup specs and color codes

wires.note: blue on some bridge pickups; tied to the bridge pickup's base plate / the neck pickup's cover

note: StewMac's chart lists Tele lead (bridge) pickups as black (or blue) start / white (or yellow) finish and rhythm (neck) pickups as black / white. Lollar: the bridge pickup's base plate is connected to the black lead, and the neck's black lead grounds the cover - which is why Tele leads must not simply be reversed.

source.title: StewMac: Pickup specs and color codes
